title: Mongla coastal communities demand climate grants, not loans
excerpt: Women, fishers and farmers rallied on the Pashur river bank, saying COP31 has produced no concrete money for salinity-hit coastal communities.
content:
Coastal women, fishers and farmers formed a human chain and held a rally on the bank of the Pashur river at Dakshin Kainmari in Mongla, demanding that climate finance be paid as grants rather than loans, The Daily Star reported on 17 November.

Mongla Nagorik Samaj, Khaddo Nirapotta Network (KHANI) and three other organisations organised the event. Speakers also demanded safe drinking water and a just transition, and said the COP31 climate talks had produced no concrete money for salinity-hit coastal communities. They asked for coastal women, fishers and farmers to have a say when the National Adaptation Plan and Bangladesh's climate pledges (NDCs) are drafted.

Speakers said disaster losses between 2015 and 2020 came to Tk 1,79,199 crore, nearly 10 times the losses of the previous six years, and that Bangladesh produces less than 0.5 percent of global emissions.

"Climate finance must not become another burden of debt," said climate activist Ratna Sheikh. Mohammad Noor Alam Sheikh, president of Mongla Nagorik Samaj, and SM Jane Alam Babu, president of Udayan Jubo Sangha, also spoke.

Why it matters

The demand for grants over loans is Bangladesh's official position at COP31 too, but this rally puts it in the words of the people who live with rising salinity. It is a reminder for NGOs and donors that locally led adaptation means giving coastal communities a real role in planning, not only in delivery.

What to watch

The final COP31 decisions on adaptation finance when the talks close on 20 November, and whether the government opens the National Adaptation Plan review to coastal community groups.
